text:
sasha: Heads-up — ran a quick fuzz of the paged bank + shard layout on the Llama-2-13B-ish model and hit an odd p99 regression when dtype==int8 and batch_size in (6..12).

alex: can you paste the exact profile? numbers + env please.

sasha: gist of results below, ran on rtx-8000-sim, kernel selector: hybrid-flash/paged-fuse v2.2.1, batching heuristic: dynamic-window (max_tokens=2048).

sasha: ```
# micro-run: concat of 10 warmups + 30 steady iters
batch_size=8, seq_len=1024, dtype=int8, kv_layout=sharded_pages
throughput: 620 tok/s (was 760 tok/s baseline)
latency_p50: 38ms, p95: 112ms, p99: 220ms (baseline p99 ~ 185ms)
mem: ~11.9GB resident, kv-page-fragmentation: 6%

ktrace: saw repeated bank-move ops at offsets aligned to 512B boundaries
```

maria: hmm bank-move + 512B alignment sounds like a mis-sharded page boundary. did the profiler capture any warp-miss spikes?

sasha: yes, warp_miss_rate jumped ~3x for the fused kernel path, and the selector fell back to flash-hybrid with extra memcpy.

jen: any chance this is due to the new compact-page allocator from the packing PR? that changed page base alignment from 4KB -> 2KB to reduce waste.

alex: that's likely — compacting reduces page padding but can create unaligned cache lines for the interleaved bank layout. we saw similar on bf16 earlier but not as noisy.

sasha: repro script attached (pseudocode):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=./bench python bench/kv_shard_test.py \
  --model llama-2-13b --dtype int8 --kv-layout sharded_pages \
  --page-size 2048 --interleave true --batch 8 --iters 40
```

maria: quick triage idea: try page-size 4096 and interleave=false (separate pages) to see if p99 normalizes. also test batch=4 and batch=16 to find threshold.

sasha: did that — results:
- page=4096 + interleave=false: throughput 748 tok/s, p99 188ms (back to baseline)
- page=2048 + interleave=false: 730 tok/s, p99 190ms
- page=2048 + interleave=true + batch=4: 745 tok/s, p99 186ms
- page=2048 + interleave=true + batch=12: 610 tok/s, p99 228ms

alex: so it's an interaction between interleaving + certain batch sizes causing stride that hits bank collision pattern. likely because int8 shrinks per-kv stride and our bank assignment modulo page_size creates repeating conflict for some batch counts.

jen: actionable: change packing PR to enforce page_base aligned to max(4KB, page_size) for interleaved layouts, or add a small random offset / linear probing when allocating shard pages to break fixed stride.

perf-bot: perf-ci run queued: bench/kv_shard_test.py with {page=2048, interleave=true, batch=[4,8,12]} on 3 GPUs. link: https://ci.internal/reports/2045/kv-shard-2048

maria: also add a quick kernel-selector flag to prefer 'separate-pages' for int8 until we have a permanent allocator fix. low-risk stopgap.

sasha: +1 for selector flag. I'll draft a tiny RFC: keep default packing but set hint: avoid interleaved when dtype width <= 1 byte and batch mod L == 0 (where L determined by page_shard_count).

alex: one more thing — check batching heuristic: dynamic-window currently biases to larger batches during steady state; small increase in concurrency could push into the bad batch sizes. Add a guard: if p99 rises >15% in realtime, decrease candidate_batch by 2 and retry.

jen: agree. we should also add a micro-benchmark harness that sweeps batch sizes and page sizes in CI for int8. catching this earlier would have prevented the regression.

sasha: I'll send the RFC + quick selector patch today, and follow up with perf CI results. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — cc @perf-bot for follow-up checks.

perf-bot: perf-ci results: 2045/kv-shard-2048 finished: regression reproduced on 2/3 machines; suggested mitigation: selector flag applied -> removes regression.

maria: perfect. create canary with selector-flag=true and monitor console token-latency dashboards next deploy.
